source: CoSAI AI Shared Responsibility Framework §3.2, Draft V0.7
party_model_note: Each model declares the two parties whose responsibility its cells describe. The four cosai-core models describe one customer receiving a service from one vendor, so their parties are customer and provider. The proposed-extension model Federated-Consortium describes peers rather than a supply chain, so its parties are the two governing domains TAP-010 defines: the Shared Commons and Participant Sovereign Assets. Read column labels and cell keys from model.parties rather than assuming customer and provider.

models.name: AI-Enabled SaaS
models.description: Provider supplies a managed AI application. Customer retains business governance and supplies context data; provider assumes technical responsibility for the application, platform, and model.

models.name: AI Platform as a Service
models.description: Customer builds and operates the application layer on a provider-managed AI platform. Customer owns business governance and the application; provider manages the platform and foundational model.

models.name: Agentic Platform as a Service
models.description: Customer owns agent definitions and business logic on a provider-managed orchestration runtime. Responsibility at L3 and L5 is shared as both parties control distinct parts of the agentic stack.

models.name: Infrastructure as a Service
models.description: Maximum customer responsibility. Customer builds and operates the application, platform, and model layers. Provider is accountable only for the physical and virtual infrastructure underpinning L4.

models.name: Federated Consortium
models.description: Institutions participate as self-governing peers rather than as customers of a vendor. Every layer splits into two governing domains: a Shared Commons that stays open and independently usable, and Participant Sovereign Assets that each participant controls unless it voluntarily contributes them. A participant runs the full stack locally and contributes only governed model-weight updates.

extension_value_note: participant-owned and commons-governed exist because neither party in a federated consortium is a customer or a provider. participant-owned carries the same weight as customer-owned, since a participant node holds the same unshared accountability a customer does. commons-governed carries the same weight as shared, since accountability rests with a collective body rather than with one organization.
